data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Within a single evaluation, the distinguishing evidence for genuine reliability gain is causal mediation: a held-out checklist (items re-derived from an orthogonal theory or sample) should produce equivalent reliability, whereas mere compliance collapses when the specific item-wording is perturbed.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the task construct is so narrow that only one set of items is diagnostic, a second checklist may fail even if the first was genuinely reliable, making this test too stringent.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If panelists trained on the first checklist have learned the underlying construct, a second checklist would test learning rather than the checklist's initial power.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal mediation via held-out items: Genuine reliability is mediated by the checklist's *latent construct* (the task-generating variables). Mere compliance is mediated by the *surface features* of the specific items.
